subject: FinEx — performance / throughput follow-up (post-call)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinEx — performance / throughput follow-up (post-call)

Alex — great to speak today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery + the follow-ups we discussed to size throughput and verify SLOs.

Summary of call:
- Primary UX: interactive account search & summary (users expect near-real-time responses) + background batch indexing jobs.
- Model: currently evaluating an instruction-tuned 7B open model for generation; interested in a quantized runtime to save cost.
- Key perf targets you mentioned: interactive SLOs (p95) in the ~150–300ms range, and the ability to stream partial responses for long summaries.

Questions / data we need to finalize throughput sizing:
1) Typical and peak concurrent users hitting the interactive route? (ballpark is fine)
2) Average request size (tokens in) and average response size (tokens out) — if you have a sample distribution, please attach.
3) Percent of calls that require streaming vs non-streaming.
4) Expected steady-state QPS and expected short-term peak QPS (e.g., during end-of-day runs or marketing spikes).
5) Any hard latency constraints for bulk/background jobs (these can be relaxed compared to interactive).

What I attached:
- finex_workload_sample.csv (sample 24h trace you uploaded)
- redwood_sizing_template.xlsx (template we use to map tokens/QPS -> GPU sizing)

Short ask: please reply with the answers above; if it's easier, your SRE can drop the 24–72h qps/tokens log (CSV). Once we have that I can run a quick sizing estimate and propose a Dedicated/Hosted plan (and whether streaming needs push us to dedicated capacity).

Next steps I propose:
- You reply with the basic numbers (1–4) or the CSV trace
- I'll produce a draft sizing doc and recommended config by EOD your timezone tomorrow
- If needed, schedule a follow-up ops call with Rafael and our infra engineer to validate concurrency/streaming behavior.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

--
Attachments: finex_workload_sample.csv, redwood_sizing_template.xlsx

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinEx SRE <sre@finex.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinEx — performance / throughput follow-up (post-call)

Thanks Neha — good summary. Answers inline and attaching a short QPS/tokens dump (finex_qps_log.csv).

Answers:
1) Concurrent users:
- Typical steady-state concurrent interactive users: ~40–60 (US region).
- Peak concurrent (marketing/quarterly reports): ~180–220 (we plan for 200).

2) Tokens:
- Average tokens in per interactive request: ~85 tokens (median ~60).
- Average tokens out per interactive response: ~140 tokens (median ~95).
- For background indexing jobs, requests are larger (~800–2,000 tokens) but tolerance for higher latency.

3) Streaming:
- ~55% of interactive calls expect streaming (progressive summary display). The rest are short single-shot responses.

4) QPS:
- Steady-state QPS (interactive): ~3–6 qps (across our global frontends for US this is ~4 qps).
- Peak QPS short bursts: up to ~28–30 qps for a few minutes, sustained peak windows up to ~2–3 minutes.

5) Background jobs:
- Can tolerate p95 up to 2–3s. Latency critical only for interactive p95.

Notes on SLOs:
- Our product team would like interactive p95 <= 250ms if possible. p99 can be relaxed but should remain < 700ms.

Attached: finex_qps_log.csv (1 week sample with timestamps, qps, avg_tokens_in, avg_tokens_out). Hope that helps — let me know if you want more granular histograms.

Best,
Alex Turner
Product Ops | FinEx
alex.turner@finex.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 02:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FinEx — performance / throughput follow-up (post-call)

Thanks — saw Alex's note and the CSV. Quick internal plan:

Short sizing takeaways (ballpark):
- With avg interactive request ~225 tokens total (in+out) and steady qps ~4, steady-state tokens/sec ~900 tokens/s (4 qps * 225 tokens).
- Peak burst (30 qps * 225) = ~6,750 tokens/s during short spikes.
- For 55% streaming, we need low tail latency and efficient KV cache + streaming optimizations.

Initial recommendation:
- Proposal: start with a small Dedicated instance (1-2 GPU nodes) using a quantized 7B/3B family depending on quality; run dedicated for streaming-sensitive routes and use Hosted fallback for background jobs.
- Autoscale policy: maintain 1 node baseline for steady load, burst to 3 nodes for peak (2–3 minute sustained peaks).
- SLA/latency tuning: request we run a short stress test (simulated 30 qps with realistic token distributions) to validate p95 <= 250ms for interactive path. Rafael to own test plan.

Next steps (internal + with customer):
- Neha: send the CSV to Rafael & DM the Drive link so I can start the sizing run.
- Rafael: I'll draft a simple test harness and propose a date for a 60-min sizing validation call (ops + FinEx SRE).
- Neha: propose two 60-min windows tomorrow (US mornings) for the validation test.

I'll prepare a short preliminary sizing doc by EOD and attach to the HubSpot deal.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
